solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boring youngster giving up drink

parts.note: PO is short for po-faced, dull and humourless, so it can stand for boring
a teen is a young person aged thirteen to nineteen

explanation.surface: A dull teenager decides to swear off alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving up' is a link here, though it tempts as a reversal sign. POTEEN is Irish illicit spirit, often spelt poitín.
explanation.definitionFit: Poteen is a strong Irish spirit traditionally distilled illegally from potatoes or grain, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Where some talk and some walk without a care

definitions.meaning: broadcasting on radio, as presenters do

explanation.surface: Some people chat, others stroll happily.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcast presenters talk while live, and the carefree are said to walk elated.

clue.text: Frenchman getting up to box noble fight

indicators.note: to box means to enclose, so the reversed name holds the other piece
in a down clue getting up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Rene is a French man's name
a count is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman rises to fight a nobleman in the boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns RENE into ENER; 'to box' means to enclose, not to spar.
explanation.definitionFit: An encounter is a battle or clash between opposing forces.

clue.text: US gateway in North East with key round-the-clock banks

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation
A is a musical key

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its edges, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An airport in the north-east with security around the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Newark Liberty is a major airport serving New York, an entry point to the US.

clue.text: Vintage recording group without repertoire

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the group word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a caste is a social group or class
a set is a performer's programme of numbers

explanation.surface: A band with no songs to play makes an old-fashioned record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but here it carries its old sense of outside, so the group word wraps the repertoire word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tape cassettes were a common recording format of the 1970s and 80s, now a retro medium.

clue.text: What a diver with eczema might do to make the grade

definitions.text: What a diver with eczema might do
definitions.meaning: a diver would surface to scratch an itchy rash

explanation.surface: A diver with an itch has to perform well.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming up to scratch is an idiom for meeting the expected standard.

clue.text: Tabloid's had European cover

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper ran a European cover story.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunshade is a parasol or awning giving cover from the sun.

clue.text: Fell over having caught heel of boot to be precise

indicators.note: over means turned upside down, so the fell word is read backwards

parts.note: to fell a tree is to axe it
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the heel of a word is its last letter, taken here from boot

explanation.surface: Someone tripped and caught their boot heel, to be specific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell over' looks like tumbling; 'over' turns AXE into EXA.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means accurate in every detail, a synonym of precise.

clue.text: The One Show tune, perhaps

parts.note: the One Show is a BBC evening magazine programme; its signature music is an example

explanation.surface: The music from a BBC TV programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme's signature tune identifies it, an example of the category.

clue.text: Now 'Ma' could be 'Mistress'

parts.note: these two words are what a fancy, that is rearranged, version of a lady would give

explanation.surface: Mother's role may have changed: she is now the lady of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: a fancy (rearranged) WOMAN would be NOW MA, which is exactly what the clue shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy woman is an old-fashioned term for a man's lover, a kept mistress.

clue.text: Lincoln's dreary opening not exactly stirring

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of President Abraham Lincoln

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, taken here from dreary

explanation.surface: Lincoln's opening speech was dull and failed to rouse anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone still lying in bed is not moving about, so is literally not stirring.

clue.text: 4×4's ornate trim

indicators.note: something ornate is elaborately reworked, so the spelt-out letters are rearranged

parts.note: the figures are written out as words: four and four

explanation.surface: An off-road vehicle has fancy decorative finishing.
explanation.walkthrough: '4×4' looks like a car but is simply spelt out as two words to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Frou-frou means fussy ornamental decoration, such as frills used to trim a dress.

clue.text: Dislike game taking time? Don't start!

indicators.note: taking means holding, so the game animal contains the other piece

parts.note: a hare is hunted as game

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, taken here from Don't

explanation.surface: Someone who hates a sport that takes too long tells you not to begin it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatred is intense dislike or loathing, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Voice pipe

definitions.meaning: to give voice to feelings is to express them openly
an outlet or duct for air or smoke

explanation.surface: A speaking tube on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: You voice or air your anger, and a flue or duct letting air out is an outlet of the same name.

clue.text: Heading off some expert hopelessly unprepared

indicators.note: hopelessly suggests muddled, so the letters are rearranged
heading off means losing the head, the first letter

explanation.surface: Some expert sets off without preparing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' removes S from SOME, leaving OME; 'hopelessly' rearranges OME with EXPERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore means spoken or done without preparation, off the cuff.

clue.text: Highly desirable editor of Loaded

indicators.note: loaded can mean drunk, so the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: The editor of the lads' magazine Loaded is a highly sought-after person.
explanation.walkthrough: Loaded was a British men's magazine; here 'Loaded' is the anagram signal on EDITOR OF.
explanation.definitionFit: Something you would give your life for is irresistibly attractive, an idiom.

clue.text: Aim an overdue shot

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Take aim at a long-delayed attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like a noun for an attempt but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an attempt or goal, so it can mean an aim.

clue.text: Bad actor tackling Noddy oddly an odd-jobber

indicators.note: tackling means taking hold of, so the actor holds the other piece

parts.note: a ham is an overacting performer

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters

explanation.surface: A poor actor takes on the role of Noddy, the children's toy character.
explanation.walkthrough: Noddy is a children's book character created by Enid Blyton. 'oddly' gives N, D, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone doing odd jobs is a jack of all trades, the classic handyperson.

clue.text: Missing inevitable conclusion arrest was bungled in film

indicators.note: something bungled is botched and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged
missing means lacking, so a letter is taken away from the following words
the conclusion of a word is its last letter, taken here from inevitable

explanation.surface: An unavoidable arrest went wrong in a cinema thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing inevitable conclusion' removes E (the end of inevitable) from ARREST WAS; 'bungled' then rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Wars is the 1977 George Lucas space opera, an example of a film.

clue.text: Where archaeologists may be found day and night?

definitions.meaning: excavation sites are where archaeologists work
rented lodgings are where you stay round the clock

explanation.surface: Archaeologists might be on site at all hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs are both excavations and informal British lodgings, where a lodger lives day and night.

clue.text: Pope's cortege includes bodyguard

indicators.note: includes means the letters sit inside the phrase

explanation.surface: The papal procession has a security detail.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort accompanies someone for protection, as a guard does.

clue.text: A second-hand mobile previously diverted

indicators.note: previously means coming before, so the mobile letter is placed ahead of the used piece

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for mobile
second-hand goods are used

explanation.surface: Someone buys a pre-owned mobile phone.
explanation.definitionFit: To be diverted is to be entertained, a synonym of being amused.

clue.text: Exercise control over beef producer

definitions.meaning: a castrated bullock raised for meat

explanation.surface: A rancher manages his cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a castrated bull raised for meat and the verb meaning to guide share this spelling.

clue.text: Cher's perversely suppressing appreciation for music study

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down, so the reordered letters contain the other piece
perversely means contrarily, so the singer's letters are put in a wrong order

parts.note: to have an ear for music is to appreciate it

explanation.surface: The singer Cher is oddly reluctant to study music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perversely' rearranges the singer's name with its 's into RESCH; an 'ear for music' is a set phrase for appreciating it.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is detailed study of a subject, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sounds like the end for computer expert

indicators.note: says the word for the end is pronounced the same as the entry

parts.note: a coda is the closing passage of a piece of music

explanation.surface: A programmer brings bad news of the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech, CODA and CODER are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A coder writes computer programs, a programmer.

clue.text: Fellow in easy street lacking any way to turn

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the two letters are removed

parts.note: to be in clover is to live in comfort, on easy street
left or right, L and R, are the ways to turn

explanation.surface: A man in a comfortable life has no direction to go.
explanation.walkthrough: COVE is old British slang for a chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Cove is dated slang for a man or chap, so a synonym for fellow.

clue.text: Space travellers do tiresome rubbish

indicators.note: rubbish suggests something thrown together badly, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Astronauts carry out dull, worthless chores.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteoroids are small rocky bodies moving through space, so they travel there.

clue.text: Trim back ditch again

parts.note: RE is a prefix meaning again
a trench is a long ditch

explanation.surface: Cut the hedge back and dig the drain once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrench is to cut back spending, so to trim back.

clue.text: Run round after belted hero in the ring

indicators.note: after means following, so the run and round pieces follow the belted piece

parts.note: belted means rushed along, as does tore
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A boxer runs round the ring after being hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belted' looks like being punched but means rushed; 'the ring' is a bullring, not a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A torero is a bullfighter, the star performer in the bullring.
